extractedFacts.wrongfulLockoutCitation: Self-help re-entry is generally available to Alabama COMMERCIAL landlords at common law (peaceable, lease-authorized). The enhanced-damages statute for wrongful lockout (Ala. Code Sec. 35-9A-407, greater of actual damages or up to 3 months' rent) is part of the Alabama Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act and does not extend to commercial tenancies. No confirmed commercial-specific statutory enhancement found; a commercial tenant's remedy for an improper lockout (e.g., breach of the peace, no lease authorization) is actual damages via common-law tort theories.

outcome.description: After a damages hearing, the Baldwin Circuit Court rendered judgment for the landlord in the amount of $94,350 plus costs of court against the tenant and guarantor (the landlord had claimed $89,010 in its summary-judgment motion and later $146,910; the tenant argued for no more than $18,900). Attorney's fees were not separately stated. The Supreme Court of Alabama affirmed both the liability determination and the damages judgment.
